name: Balenciaga
why: Oversized, experimental clothing built on couture technique, from the Paris house.
origin: Founded by Cristóbal Balenciaga; the Paris house opened in 1937.

notes.fren: a Paris house that traded elegance for irony — Frenchness as raw material
notes.street: a couture house running drop culture — the Triple S made ugly luxury street law
notes.weird: Deliberately ugly as a strategy, and the weirdness is corporate and calculated rather than personal. That does not make it less effective — it makes it a different kind of strange.
notes.status: Status through provocation rather than through beauty. The logo, the deliberately ugly silhouette and the joke pricing are the same gesture, and the wearer is signalling that they are in on it.

craft_evidence.owned_d: LEATHER GOODS ONLY, and only part of them. 'The Plant', Cerreto Guidi (Florence, Tuscany) is owned by Balenciaga (a Kering house); FashionNetwork describes it as its first owned production site, and International Leather Maker (10 Feb 2026) as its 'first in-house leather goods production facility'. The site is a revived 1960s leather workshop of ~10,000 m2, announced in 2020 for a 2021 opening, with a training centre. LaConceria quotes CEO Gianfranco Gianangeli saying 100% of leather goods are made in Tuscany 'with suppliers', and reports 176 staff, with 'a significant part' of production to be internalised progressively. Balenciaga said it 'will continue to rely on its current network of local suppliers'. No owned RTW or footwear facility found.
